decisions.reason: As a newly launched lever-handle family in a design-driven, broad-range portfolio, it is still an inexpensive option to keep open while market acceptance becomes clearer.
The mitred variant is somewhat more niche and may face overlap with other handle families, but after only one year the firm would likely keep it on the market to learn more about demand.
Its multifunctional positioning fits the firm's accessibility and system-solution strategy, so management would likely preserve the option until customer uptake is better revealed.
Because this is a relatively generic new door lever in a crowded internal assortment, it has a higher pruning risk, yet the evidence is still too limited for immediate abandonment.
A separately promoted new collection with a 2023 German Design Award sends a strong positive signal, making withdrawal within the next year unlikely.
A new finish is usually low-cost to maintain and supports the firm's architecture-oriented offering, so it would likely be retained unless demand quickly proves weak.
